title: In-Storage Domain-Specific Acceleration for Serverless Computing
problem: For serverless functions in datacenters with storage disaggregation and hardware accelerators, the overhead of accessing disaggregated storage overwhelms the performance gains from accelerators, preventing effective combination of these three infrastructure trends.
motivation: Modern datacenters are simultaneously adopting serverless computing, storage disaggregation, and domain-specific accelerators; efficiently combining these trends is critical for maximizing datacenter performance and efficiency.
method: DSCS-Serverless places a programmable accelerator (hardware customized for specific tasks) directly inside the storage device with a 25-watt power budget. In disaggregated systems where compute and storage are separate, accessing remote storage creates latency overhead that overwhelms accelerator benefits—but by co-locating the accelerator with storage instead of using conventional approaches like ARM cores or FPGAs, this design eliminates the access delay that normally dominates performance.
key_novelty: A programmable accelerator embedded within the storage device itself lets serverless functions use acceleration without the latency penalty of accessing remote storage.
contributions: DSCS-Serverless architecture embedding accelerators in storage to eliminate access latency
Achieves 3.7× speedup over ARM-based computational storage and 1.7× over Xilinx FPGA designs
Reduces energy consumption by 4.3× versus ARM and 1.9× versus FPGA approaches
Demonstrates 3.2× better cost efficiency over ARM and 2.3× over FPGA-based computational storage
